title: Agent Client Protocol (ACP)
subtitle: I built agents that speak the Agent Client Protocol so coding assistants can be driven as governed workers rather than chat windows.

stats.label: hard ceiling on delegation depth; a persona configured deeper is refused
checks on every receipt: audience, issuer, hash and call chain
transports for the same envelopes: stdio and Redis streams
typed endings in the delivery adapter besides acceptance

lede: ACP is the seam between my governance platform and the vendors' own tools. Agent Swarm lets agents delegate to one another, and a receiving agent has to know who really sent a request, on whose behalf, and that the chain of delegation is not looping or growing without end. I did not want a home-grown protocol for that. I adopted the Agent Client Protocol, which is JSON-RPC 2.0, as the cross-vendor agent protocol and locked the choice into the runtime's master plan; I did not author ACP, I use it and extend it.
quote: I put identity and delegation limits into the wire itself.
evidence: Agent-to-agent protocol design: the Agent Client Protocol adopted as the cross-vendor wire and extended with canonical hashing and RS256-signed envelopes, keeping the base protocol standard.
Multi-agent governance: bounded delegation enforced on every receipt with 4 checks (audience, issuer, hash and call chain) and a hard depth ceiling of 25 that no persona can raise.

Agent orchestration: a delivery adapter that drives a vendor's own coding tool through its supported ACP bridge and counts a prompt accepted only on the vendor's own acknowledgement, with 7 typed endings.
author: Corey James
